title: The Sound That Broke the World
hook: You think the loudest sounds are nearby, but one traveled 3,000 miles.
script: You think the loudest sounds are nearby, but one traveled 3,000 miles. In 1883, the Krakatoa eruption created a noise so extreme it broke the scale. What happens when a sound is powerful enough to travel around the world? It stops being a noise and becomes a pressure wave. This wave was so intense it circled the globe seven times over five days. Sailors 40 miles away had their eardrums ruptured instantly. The blast released energy equal to 13,000 Hiroshima bombs. This energy pushed the ocean back, triggering tsunamis 120 feet high. It even turned the sun blue for years by veiling the stratosphere in sulfur. Send this to the friend who thinks they've heard it all.
